ev.cutoff_tip: The organiser's cutoff (hours). When set, the feasibility check compares the race calculator's predicted finish with it.
ev.turnaround_tip: Turn back if the summit isn't reached this many hours after starting on summit day. The feasibility check compares the predicted time to the summit with it; too late = not a fit for this Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) route.
feas.title: Race check
feas.sub: Each race: is there time to get ready, and are you ready now
ev.dayplan_help: Without a GPX, fill in each day's distance and climb (descent optional: blank = same as the climb); the totals add up by themselves. A GPX with each day's end marked wins over these numbers.
ev.dayplan_missing: Please add each day's distance and climb
ev.dayplan_old: This older trip has no distance and climb for each day yet; you can save it as it is, and edit its total distance and climb directly. Until they are added, each day is taken as an equal share of the totals, so adding them is more accurate. To add them, fill in every day's distance and climb.
ev.format_tip: Stages: one stage a day, set by the organiser — fill in each stage's distance and climb. Non-stop: one course, you decide where to sleep — no per-day numbers; add sleep points to the aid stations in the race calculator instead.
ev.gpx_missing: Upload a GPX for an ultra: the build-phase climb sessions and the race check need it to know where the climbing is
ev.poles_tip: When ticked, the race calculator adds a short poles note on steep climbs and steep descents (≤ −15 %). The predicted time, pace and heart rate don't change: studies show poles mainly make it feel easier and take load off the knees, at about the same speed. The activities of the race day (each day of a multi-day trip) are also preset to "With poles"; any you set yourself stay as you set them.
ev.trail_pct_tip: The share of the course on dirt or trail (not asphalt or concrete). ≥ 50%: the Build phase gets one technical-terrain session a week close to the race's footing; < 50%: the course is mostly paved, no such session; blank: as before (one a week).
ev.gpx_later: I'll upload the GPX later — skip the days for now
ev.gpx_help: With a GPX (or "upload later" ticked) you don't type each day: each day's distance and climb come from the GPX. Once saved, press the trip's "Days" (or "Day split preview" in the race calculator) to set where each day ends (camp waypoints, OSM huts and the nights of a recording are listed as candidates; a Cairn import's overnight stops are applied as they are); until then each day is an equal share of the distance (estimate).
ev.gpx_have: GPX attached ({f}): each day's numbers come from it — the rows are optional
ev.gpx_nosplit: The GPX has no day ends yet: each day is an equal share of the distance for now (estimate). Open this race in the Race manager and press "Days" to set where each day ends
ev.cairn_attach: Or paste a Cairn share link
ev.cairn_tip: Paste the link from the route's Share in Cairn: the GPX is imported and the overnight stops marked in Cairn become each day's end (the days follow); change them later with "Days"
ev.cairn_prompt: Paste the Cairn route's share link (https://…/?gpx=…&share=…)
ev.cairn_from: This GPX was imported from Cairn: open the route in Cairn
ev.priority_help: A = main goal (the phases count back from it). B = secondary: with an A race ahead, a 5-day mini-taper before it and a recovery by its size after it, the phases unchanged; with no A race, a 4-week light prep + a 1-week taper before it. C = training (replaces a hard session or the long run), the phases unchanged.
ev.priority_help_n: A = main goal (the phases count back from it). B = secondary: with an A race ahead, a 5-day mini-taper before it and a recovery by its size after it, the phases unchanged; with no A race, a {w}-week light prep + a {d}-day taper before it (estimate). C = training (replaces a hard session or the long run), the phases unchanged.
guide.maintain_ctl: Chronic load flat, no longer raised
guide.maintain_vt2: One hard session a week: zone 5 (above VT2); road runners take zone 3 in the threshold block
guide.maintain_rest: A recovery week at least every 6 weeks
tl.specific_src: Why {n} {n|week|weeks} of Build: Uphill Athlete's 20-week intro-to-ultra template has 8 running-specific weeks + a 2-week taper, the same as here; Pfitzinger's marathon about 8 weeks, Canova 6–8 weeks, Daniels' last phase 6 weeks, Yen-Ching Chiang's specific peak about 1.5 months before a race of 4 hours or more (coaches' advice). 2 of those weeks are recovery weeks.

ev.add_in_races: Add one in the Race manager →

guide.recovery_1: Acute load down, load balance back above zero
guide.base_2: EF (speed at the same heart rate) going up
guide.specific_1: VAM (climbing faster at the same heart rate)
guide.specific_2: Climb per km close to the target
guide.specific_3: Longest session nearing the target time
guide.specific_4: Less drift late in long sessions
guide.taper_1: Weekly hours down to 40–60% of usual
guide.taper_3: Load balance back above zero, chronic load only slightly down

tl.mini_taper: B race mini-taper: no intervals in the 5 days before, no tempo or long runs in the 4 days before
tl.auto: Automatic: a {taper}-day taper before each A race ({baiyue} {baiyue|day|days} for a multi-day Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) trip, {baiyue_long} {baiyue_long|day|days} for 4 days or more{pref}), {weeks} {weeks|week|weeks} of Build before that, Base for the rest; after a race 1 week of recovery, plus 1 week of rebuild for a marathon-size race, 2 weeks of recovery for an ultra, 2 weeks of recovery + 2 of rebuild for a 100-miler (ultra: predicted ≥ {hours} {hours|hour|hours} — the race calculator first, then the time you entered; with neither, effort distance EP ≥ {ep} (km plus climb converted); multi-day trips count too); a race with far more descent than you trained in the last 6 weeks gets one more level of recovery. The rebuild comes after the transition, easy runs and strength only.
